comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Swept, and the name stays `muster`.** Nothing found is well enough known to be worth a rename, which was the call this card existed to make.

What is out there, so the next person asking does not sweep it again:

- **crates.io** holds `muster` and `muster-cli` (`scott2b/muster`, "terminal session group management built on tmux", 195 and 112 downloads), and `muster-workspace` (`sagoez/muster`, "a terminal workspace for running CLI agents and dev processes side by side", v0.8.0, 175 downloads). The last of those is the closest thing to a collision anywhere - very nearly this project's own one-line pitch - and it is still a crate almost nobody has installed.
- **npm** has `@musterhq/cli` ("governed agent harness for production AI agents"), a `@dws/muster-*` family, and a plain `muster` that validates objects in JavaScript.
- **GitHub** has `giantswarm/muster` (MCP tool management), `facebookarchive/muster`, `json4s/muster`, `llnl/muster` and others, none in this space and none active in it.
- **Homebrew core is clear**, and a tap namespaces the install regardless: `brew install amterp/tap/muster`.

The download counts are the whole argument. Three digits on the nearest neighbour means the name is shared rather than taken, and sharing it costs less than an `fr` sweep across a repo this size plus every doc, config key and binary name in it.

Worth knowing rather than acted on: `muster-cli` is both this repo's own binary name and a published crate. Nothing in Muster publishes to crates.io (`publish = false`), so the two never meet - but that is the one place a future decision to publish a crate would run into this.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: Sweep brew, crates, npm, GitHub for 'muster' clashes in the terminal/devtool space. Renaming is cheap now (fr sweep), expensive after a release.
title: Name-collision check before going public
